limits: `bgp_prefixes` counts the neighbor's `received-routes`, which on SR Linux 26.7.2 includes routes that fail BGP loop detection and are not usable. On a live capture of `examples/srl-frr` on 2026-10-28 the counter read 3 where one prefix was usable and `rejected-routes` read 0. A `min` or `exact` prefix check on SR Linux can pass on a count that includes unusable routes. The test data above predates that capture; it has not yet been re-captured. Mitigation: pair the count with `route` checks for the prefixes that matter. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

graceful restart: a stale path (a restarting peer's route, kept until it re-sends it or the stale timer ends) counts as present and best; no stale marker is read yet. A route check can pass on a route that is about to go. Mitigation: leave graceful restart off in the lab, or use a `timeout` above the stale timer. Fix scheduled: 0.4.1.

startup config: a line the NOS rejects at boot isn't detected yet, so the lab can run without it. Config applied with `setup:` commands is checked. Mitigation: add a positive check for what each changed line creates. Fix scheduled: 0.4.

Hidden routes count as received, except routes Junos hid because the import policy rejected them (`hidden-reason` "Rejected by import policy"): those can never be used, and FRR and Arista EOS don't keep them at all.
`bgp_route` reads routes received over BGP only. Junos doesn't list its own static, direct or aggregate routes as BGP routes, even when an export policy advertises them.
`bgp_prefixes` reads Junos's `accepted-prefix-count`, which also leaves out received routes Junos can't use (an unusable next hop); FRR counts those.
Link and node faults on a cJunosEvolved node and `inject_routes` from it are refused before deploying.

Every deploy installs Junos in the VM: about 4 minutes to a CLI on a quiet 20-thread host, up to 19 minutes with a CPU-heavy job beside it. Set `CPTX_NUM_IF` (see the example) and a check `timeout` that covers the boot.
